(i) $(\sin \theta)^2 + (\cos \theta)^2 = \left(\frac{PM}{OP}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{OM}{OP}\right)^2$

$$= \frac{PM^2}{OP^2} + \frac{OM^2}{OP^2} = \frac{PM^2 + OM^2}{OP^2} = \frac{OP^2}{OP^2} \text{ [by the formula of Pythagoras]}$$

$$= 1$$

Or, $(\sin \theta)^2 + (\cos \theta)^2 = 1$

$$\therefore \boxed{(\sin \theta)^2 + (\cos \theta)^2 = 1}$$

**Remarks:** For integer indices $n$ we can write $\sin^n \theta$ for $(\sin \theta)^n$ and $\cos^n \theta$ for $(\cos \theta)^n$.

(ii) $\sec^2 \theta = (\sec \theta)^2 = \left(\frac{OP}{OM}\right)^2$

$$= \frac{OP^2}{OM^2} = \frac{OM^2 + PM^2}{OM^2} \text{ [OP is the hypotenuse of right-angled } \triangle POM]$$

$$= \frac{OM^2}{OM^2} + \frac{PM^2}{OM^2}$$

$$= 1 + \left(\frac{PM}{OM}\right)^2 = 1 + (\tan \theta)^2 = 1 + \tan^2 \theta$$

$$\therefore \boxed{\sec^2 \theta - \tan^2 \theta = 1} \text{ and } \boxed{\tan^2 \theta = \sec^2 \theta - 1}$$

(iii) $\text{cosec}^2 \theta = (\text{cosec} \theta)^2 = \left(\frac{OP}{PM}\right)^2$

$$= \frac{OP^2}{PM^2} = \frac{PM^2 + OM^2}{PM^2} \text{ [OP is the hypotenuse of right-angled } \triangle POM]$$

$$= \frac{PM^2}{PM^2} + \frac{OM^2}{PM^2} = 1 + \left(\frac{OM}{PM}\right)^2$$

$$= 1 + (\cot \theta)^2 = 1 + \cot^2 \theta$$

$$\therefore \boxed{\text{cosec}^2 \theta - \cot^2 \theta = 1} \text{ and } \boxed{\cot^2 \theta = \text{cosec}^2 \theta - 1}$$

**Example 3.** If $\tan A = \frac{4}{3}$, find the other trigonometric ratios of the angle $A$.

**Solution:** Given that, $\tan A = \frac{4}{3}$
